# Test index {#sec-appc}

This index helps you find the CTest command that runs a test. A row identifies a registered command, not an
individual assertion or a successful run. Use the inventory to select a command, then read its test source for
the cases, tolerances and skip conditions.

C++ tests are registered through `setup_test`. The macro builds an executable and gives its CTest entry the
same name, with the lower-case build type appended. Thus a Release configuration produces the `.release`
suffix ({{< code cmake/macros/macro_setup_test.cmake >}}). One such executable can contain multiple
GoogleTest cases; its single inventory row is not a case count.

For Python, `subprocess_tests` groups the files whose native calls already run in child processes into the
single CTest entry `test_python_subprocess`. The remaining `test*.py` files receive separate entries named
by filename. The `list(REMOVE_ITEM ...)` step excludes the grouped files from that second registration loop
({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}).

For example, `test_latent_heat_sign.py` belongs to `subprocess_tests`. To select its CTest group, use
`test_python_subprocess`; absence of a separate row for that filename does not mean CTest omits it
({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}). Conversely, the commented-out `test_yaml_parse` and `test_kinetics_rates`
setup lines do not register commands ({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}).

From an already configured build directory, list commands before running the selected entry. For example,
`test_python_subprocess` is the grouped entry defined by `add_test` ({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}):

```bash
ctest -N
ctest -R '^test_python_subprocess$' --output-on-failure
```

The anchors in the regular expression select the exact name. The first command lists registrations; the
second executes the selected command. These are usage instructions, not a recorded test run.

The generated inventory below records its configuration. Match that configuration when comparing inventories,
and use the names printed by your own `ctest -N` when choosing a test.

Registration does not establish device coverage. `DeviceTest::SetUp` skips a CUDA parameter when
`torch::cuda::is_available()` is false and an MPS parameter when `torch::hasMPS()` is false
({{< code tests/device_testing.hpp DeviceTest::SetUp >}}). The module-level `pytestmark` in the workspace test
also skips when CUDA is unavailable ({{< code tests/test_cuda_workspace.py pytestmark >}}).
These conditions describe the test source; they are not observations from an execution.

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Not provided: per-case pass counts, measured errors, timings and CPU/CUDA coverage, because this inventory
records registration rather than test execution. A registered command may contain skipped cases. Its name
alone does not establish which assertions ran or whether their tolerances were met.
:::
